card.goal: Add caching to the product API

items.ask: Which cache should the product API use?

exchange.person:
Remind me what this question you asked me is about: why it came up, and what each choice would mean. Don't act on it yet.
"Which cache should the product API use?"
Options: Redis / In-memory
exchange.reply:
This came up because /products takes 900 ms at p95, almost all of it in the same three queries.

- **Redis**: a shared cache across all four API instances. Cache hits stay consistent, and a deploy doesn't empty it. It adds a service to run and about 1 ms per lookup.
- **In-memory**: each instance keeps its own LRU. No new service, and lookups are near free. But each instance warms separately, and a price change can show stale for up to the TTL on some instances.

I'd go with Redis: prices change during the day, and stale prices on some instances would confuse customers. I haven't changed anything yet.

findings.title: Staging recorded the PR's migrations under their old filenames
findings.detail: A plain migrate apply would try to add the same columns again.

exchange.person: what does that finding mean for the next deploy?
exchange.reply:
**The next deploy is safe as it stands.** The deploy branch still uses the old filenames, so staging sees nothing new to apply.

**The problem comes later.** Once the renamed migrations land on main, staging will see two new filenames and try to add the same columns again.

The fix is option 1: mark the renamed migrations as applied on staging before that deploy. You own staging, so you run it.

If you agree, I'll rewrite f221 to say exactly that: when to act, the option 1 commands, and that you run them. I'll also add a line to the rollout checklist. No code changes are needed.
